extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants involved in ex parte appeals (and counsel handling related judicial review)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing ex parte appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including who may appeal, timing, fees, required documents, pre-appeal review, interviews, record content, remands, and procedures for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable vs petitionable matters (line of demarcation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, rejections are appealable to the Board and objections are petitionable to the Director; when an objection is 'determinative of the rejection' the Board may address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the line carefully: Board will not ordinarily hear matters that should be decided by the Director on petition, and the Director will not ordinarily entertain petitions where the question is appealable to the Board. Examples of petitionable, not appealable matters include restriction finality, non-entry of election of species, amendments, and holdings of abandonment. See In re Hengehold and Ex parte Frye. Petitions not filed within 2 months may be dismissed as untimely (37 CFR 1.181(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Board and panel size
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board consists of the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioners, and administrative patent judges; appeals and contested cases are heard by at least three Board members designated by the Director (35 U.S.C. 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative patent judges should be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability appointed as provided. Treat references to predecessor Boards (BPAI) as references to the PTAB for citation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing procedure for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: When ready for docketing, the Board will (A) assign an appeal number, (B) issue a docketing notice, and (C) assign the appeal to a master docket or directly to a panel; if not docketable, the appeal will be remanded to the examining corps with an order explaining why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docketing notice or remand order notifies appellant and examiner whether the appeal is under Board jurisdiction or returned to the examining corps to resolve matters prior to decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case status continued on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application made special and advanced out of turn continues to be special throughout prosecution, including appeal, if applicant remains diligent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to make special after Board jurisdiction is transferred may be addressed to the Board and will not be granted unless the brief has been filed and applicant makes the same showing required by 37 CFR 1.102. Diligent prosecution is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal and how to file a notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant any of whose claims has been twice rejected may appeal by filing a notice of appeal and required fee (37 CFR 41.31 and 35 U.S.C. 134); patent owners in reexamination have analogous rights under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal is taken by filing the notice with the fee set in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) within time provided under 37 CFR 1.134 (extendable). Use a separate letter (form PTO/SB/31 or PTO/AIA/31 recommended). Signature of the notice is not required but other enclosed papers may require signatures; unsigned authorizations to charge fees render the notice unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing notice of appeal and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be filed within the reply period set in the last Office action (normally three months), may be filed up to six months with an appropriate petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 is filed and a notice of appeal is filed before examiner considers the reply, the notice is premature/defective; applicant must wait until the Office action in response to the reply and then may file an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal presumed to be from rejection of all claims under rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken it is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless cancelled by amendment entered by the Office (37 CFR 41.31(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not cancel claims they do not wish to appeal and also fails to argue those claims in the brief, any challenge to those rejections is waived and the Board may affirm rejections against such claims (see Hyatt v. Dudas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fees and payment limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees exist for filing notice of appeal, filing an appeal brief, requesting oral hearing, and forwarding an appeal to the Board after Examiner’s Answer; some fees have been adjusted and certain payments cannot be made via general deposit account authorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(6) and 37 CFR 41.20(b). Appeal-brief filing fee was set to $0 effective March 19, 2013; forwarding fee added at 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4). Appeal fees due under 37 CFR 41.20 cannot be paid using a general authorization under 37 CFR 1.25(b) (which only authorizes payment under 1.16–1.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief filing time and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant must file an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 within the time set (generally within two months of filing the notice of appeal) and adhere to the content and format rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 19, 2013 the fee for filing an appeal brief was set at $0, and for as long as it remains $0 briefs are not defective for failure to pay or make statements about the fee. Time for filing the brief is extendible under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of appeal are reviewed by the Patent Appeal Center; if defective the Office will notify applicant. Defects include untimeliness, untimely payment of required fees, or premature filing when replies under 1.111 have been filed but not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications about defects are handled by the Patent Appeal Center (e.g., PTOL-461). In rare events where defects are identified after entry, the examiner should contact the Patent Appeal Center to determine appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of appeal after reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is reopened after filing a notice of appeal and before a Board decision, appellant must file a new notice of appeal and a complete new appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and 41.37 to reinstate the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously paid appeal fees need not be paid again except where a final Board decision has been made; if fees have increased, appellant must pay the difference. The new appeal brief must be filed within two months from the new notice date (extendible). If the prior appeal resulted in a written decision, full fees are required for any later new appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Review Request filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-appeal brief review request may be filed upon filing a notice of appeal (pilot program): it must be filed with the notice, before filing an appeal brief, use Form PTO/AIA/33, include a separate 'Pre-Appeal Brief Request for Review' paper with arguments not exceeding five total pages, and be limited to appealable matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request failing these requirements is dismissed and cannot be corrected/resubmitted (because it would not be filed on the same date as the notice of appeal). No fees required; requests do not apply to reexamination proceedings; requests are limited to appealable, not petitionable matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Review panel composition and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated panel (including at least a supervisor and the examiner of record) will review the request and may (A) determine the application remains under appeal, (B) reopen prosecution, (C) allow the application on existing claims, or (D) dismiss the request for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel has authority to reopen prosecution and may propose a corrective amendment. Applicant is not allowed to attend the review and no interviews are granted prior to issuance of the pre-appeal decision. Filing certain subsequent papers (appeal brief, RCE, after-final amendment, affidavit/evidence, or express abandonment) prior to panel decision terminates the panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of appeal — permitted and restricted situations
rubrics_metrics.description: One interview after final rejection is normally permitted (time from mailing of final rejection through filing of appeal brief). No interviews are allowed from filing of a pre-appeal request through issuance of that decision; generally no interviews after an appeal brief is filed; interviews after Examiner’s Answer but prior to forwarding fee are usually not permitted except in unusual circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews after Board jurisdiction should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a showing in writing of extraordinary circumstances justifying a remand. Unusual circumstances may include wanting to cancel all appealed claims to proceed to allowance or where the examiner is convinced some previously rejected claims are in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Record on appeal — definition of 'Record' and 'Evidence'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Record' consists of the items listed in the content listing of the Image File Wrapper (IFW) or official file, excluding amendments, evidence, and other documents that were not entered or indicated as considered by the examiner; for appeal purposes 'Evidence' does not include dictionaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion of non-entered documents reflects that refusal to enter an amendment/evidence is petitionable and not reviewable by the Board. IDS references indicated as considered by the examiner (or listed on PTO-892) are included in the Record even if not separately appearing in the IFW content listing. IFW content listing may point to physical artifacts (original drawings, sequence listings) maintained elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission events that terminate pre-appeal review
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-appeal review panel’s review is terminated if, after filing the request but before panel decision, the applicant files an appeal brief, requests continued examination (RCE), files an after-final amendment, files an affidavit or other evidence, or expressly abandons the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After panel decision, appeal brief filing time is reset to one month from mailing of decision or the balance of the two-month period from notice of appeal, whichever is greater; extension available under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file appeal brief results in dismissal of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal brief is not filed within the time designated by 37 CFR 41.37, the applicant will be notified that the appeal stands dismissed (see MPEP § 1215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time periods may be extendible as provided by rules where applicable; reinstatement options and consequences are described elsewhere in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments, affidavits, and evidence filed with or after appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps retains jurisdiction to consider entry of amendments, affidavits, and evidence filed after final or after notice of appeal until jurisdiction passes to the Board (upon filing of a reply brief or expiration of time to file one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdiction transfers to the Board upon filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 or expiration of the time to file a reply (37 CFR 41.35). The Patent Appeal Center forwards the application to the Board after jurisdiction transfers and after processing appeal forwarding fee where waiver doesn’t apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements and consequences for notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature requirements of 1.33 and 11.18(a) do not apply to the notice of appeal filed under 37 CFR 41.31, so notices need not be signed; however, unsigned notices that include unsigned authorizations (e.g., to charge a deposit account) can render the notice unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination of signature requirement for notice of appeal does not affect requirements for other papers submitted with the notice. Use of a separate letter for the notice of appeal is strongly recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals in reexamination proceedings – distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination appeals are primarily governed by 37 CFR 41.30–41.54 and this chapter; appeals in inter partes reexamination are governed by 37 CFR 41.60–41.81 and MPEP §§ 2674–2683 and 37 CFR 41.30–41.54 are not applicable to inter partes reexamination appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners in ex parte reexamination filed before Nov 29, 1999 may appeal after second rejection; those in ex parte reexamination filed on/after Nov 29, 1999 may appeal only after final rejection of one or more claims. Failure to file appeal in ex parte reexamination can result in issuance of a reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of court papers in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor either by hand between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. EST at specified address or by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5(b) FRCP and Rule 25(b) FRAP require service on counsel if party is represented. The mail service address must not be supplemented to refer to the Director or USPTO; noncourt papers mailed to this address will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for appeals to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: To appeal to the Federal Circuit, appellant must file in the USPTO a written notice of appeal directed to the Director within the time prescribed (no less than 60 days after decision), file a copy with the Board per 37 CFR 41.10/42.6, and file a copy and pay docket fee with the Clerk of the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit is timely if it actually reaches the USPTO within time specified in 37 CFR 90.3 (including extensions) or is mailed by Priority Mail Express® in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 and 90.3. Do not mail notice of appeal to Director, Board, examiner, or Solicitor mail service address; use specified filing methods (mail, Priority Mail Express®, or hand delivery as provided in 37 CFR 104.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following Federal Circuit decision (mandate effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Federal Circuit issues its mandate, the certified decision is entered in the file and marks termination of the appeal; Office action depends on whether all claims remain rejected, some claims allowed, remand required, or reopening of prosecution is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims remain rejected, proceedings terminate and application is ordinarily abandoned; if some claims allowed, examiner may convert dependent claims to independent form or set a two-month period for applicant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form. Any Office action proposing to reopen prosecution after a court decision must be forwarded for written approval.
